metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from 48 colony files of the 1867 Colonial Office List. All historical spellings preserved as found in source documents. Extracted entities include geographic locations, administrative personnel, governmental institutions, economic data, infrastructure, demographics, and historical events.

places.name: Antigua
places.description: An island situated in W. long. 61° 45', and N. lat. 17° 6'. It is about 54 miles in circumference. Discovered by Columbus in 1493, who named it after a church in Seville, called Santa Maria La Antigua.

places.name: St. John's
places.description: The chief town in Antigua where the Governor-in-Chief of the Leeward Islands resides

places.name: Bahamas
places.description: A chain of islands lying between 21° and 27° 30' N. lat., and 70° 30' and 79° 5' W. long. The group is composed of about 20 inhabited islands and an immense number of islets and rocks.

places.name: Nassau
places.description: The capital of the Bahamas, located on New Providence island

places.name: New Providence
places.description: Island containing the capital, Nassau

places.name: Barbados
places.description: Is situated in latitude 13° 4' North and longitude 59° 37' West, and is the most windward of the Caribbee Islands. It is nearly 21 English miles long by 14 in breadth, and is said to contain a superficial area of 106,470 acres.

places.name: Bridgetown
places.description: The chief town and port, situated in the parish of St. Michael, with a population of 18,957 according to the last census

places.name: Carlisle Bay
places.description: The harbour of Barbados, an open roadstead exposed to winds from the south and south-west

places.name: Bermudas
places.description: Or Somers' Islands, a cluster of about 300 small islands, situated on the western side of the Atlantic Ocean, at a distance of about 580 miles from the nearest land, at Cape Hatteras in North Carolina

places.name: Hamilton
places.description: The present seat of Government, situated on the main island

places.name: British Columbia
places.description: Situated on the north-west coast of North America. It comprises the territory lying between the Rocky Mountains and the Pacific Ocean, extending from the United States frontier to the Simpson and Finlay rivers. Average breadth about 250 miles, coast line about 450 miles.

places.name: New Westminster
places.description: Principal settlement in British Columbia

places.name: British Guiana
places.description: A portion of the South American continent, extending from east to west about 200 miles. It includes the settlements of Demerara, Essequebo, and Berbice. Bounded on the east by Dutch Guiana (River Corentyn), on the south by Brazil, on the west by Venezuela, and on the north by the Atlantic Ocean.

places.name: Georgetown
places.description: The metropolis of British Guiana, formerly called Stabroek. Seat of Government established in 1789 for the United provinces of Demerara and Essequebo

places.name: Bulama
places.description: The Island of Bulama is situated at the entrance of the two large rivers Jeba and Rio Grande. Its distance from the Gambia is 250 miles, and from Sierra Leone 350 miles. A dependency of Sierra Leone, ceded to the British Government in 1732.

places.name: Canada
places.description: This vast territory lies principally in a N.E. and S.W. direction along the north side of the St. Lawrence and the north and east sides of lakes Ontario, Erie, Huron, and Superior. Total area 121,260 for Upper Canada, and 210,020 for Lower Canada.

places.name: Quebec
places.description: The first settlement, founded in 1608. Succumbed to British forces under General Wolfe in 1759

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.description: The Cape Colony is washed by the Atlantic and the Southern or Indian Oceans on the west and south; bounded on the north by the Gariep or Orangeriver, on the north-east by the territory of the Basutos, on the east by Kaffirland, and including what was formerly the Colony of British Kaffaria.

provenance.notes: Source file not found: output_2/1867_manual_parsed/CAPE.md

places.name: Cape Town
places.description: The capital of the Colony and the seat of Government, built between Table Bay and Table Mountain at the foot of the latter. Table Mountain rises 3,582 feet above the sea. The town is well laid out and contains numerous public buildings and several good squares.

provenance.notes: Source file not found: output_2/1867_manual_parsed/CAPE.md

places.name: Ceylon
places.description: An island situated in the Indian Ocean, off the southern extremity of Hindostan. Extreme length from north to south (Point Palmyra to Dondera Head) is 266 miles; greatest width 140 miles from Colombo to Sangemankande.

places.name: Colombo
places.description: Major city on the west coast of Ceylon

places.name: Dominica
places.description: An island situated in the centre of the Caribbean Sea, 29 miles long and 16 broad; very mountainous and picturesque. Discovered by Christopher Columbus on Sunday, 3rd November 1493.

places.name: Roseau
places.description: The capital of Dominica

places.name: Falkland Islands
places.description: Situated in the South Atlantic Ocean, consisting of the East Falkland (3,000 square miles), the West Falkland (2,300 square miles), and about 100 small islands (1,200 square miles). Mount Adam rises 2,315 feet above sea level.

provenance.notes: Source file not found: output_2/1867_manual_parsed/FALKLAND.md

places.name: Gibraltar
places.description: Under the control of the Secretary of State for War, with exception of the Convict Establishment

places.name: Gold Coast
places.description: A portion of Upper Guinea, between 5° and 4° 20' E. long., stretching along the Gulf of Guinea from the River Assini to the River Volta. British influence extends over an area of 6,000 to 8,000 square miles with a population of 250,000 to 400,000.

places.name: Cape Coast Castle
places.description: Principal British settlement and administrative center on the Gold Coast

places.name: Grenada
places.description: Situated between the parallels of 12° 30' and 11° 58' N. lat., about 21 miles in length, 12 miles in greatest breadth. Lies 68 miles S.S.W. of St. Vincent. Mountainous and very picturesque, abounding in streams and mineral springs.

places.name: St. George's
places.description: The chief town and port of Grenada

places.name: Carriacou
places.description: The largest of the Grenadines attached to Grenada, with a population of 3,071 souls

places.name: Heligoland
places.description: An island situated in the North Sea, opposite and about 25 miles from the mouth of the Elbe. Area, inclusive of the adjacent island termed 'Sandy', three-quarters of a square mile.

places.name: British Honduras
places.description: A colony on the east coast of Central America, bounded on the north by Mexican Yucatan, on the west and south by Guatemala, and on the east by the Bay of Honduras. The coast was discovered in 1502 by Columbus.

places.name: Belize
places.description: The principal settlement of British Honduras

places.name: Hong Kong
places.description: One of a number of islands called by the Portuguese 'Ladrones', situated off the south-eastern coast of China at the mouth of the Canton River, about 40 miles east of Macao. Length about 11 miles, breadth 2 to 5 miles. First ceded to Great Britain in January 1841, confirmed by Treaty of Nankin in August 1842.

places.name: Jamaica
places.description: An Island situated in the Caribbean Sea, to the southward of the eastern extremity of Cuba. The largest and formerly the most valuable of the British West Indies; 140 miles in length, and 50 in extreme breadth. Discovered by Columbus on 3rd May 1494, who called it St. Jago.

places.name: Kingston
places.description: Principal city of Jamaica with a medium heat of about 80° and minimum 70° Fahrenheit throughout the year

events.description: Antigua discovered by Columbus who named it after a church in Seville called Santa Maria La Antigua
First inhabited by a few English
Charles II made a formal grant of this island to Lord Willoughby, who sent out a large number of colonists
Declared a British possession by the Treaty of Breda after an interval of French occupation
St. Salvador was the first land discovered by Columbus on his voyage
New Providence was settled by the English and held till 1641
Bahamas were finally confirmed to Great Britain by the Peace of Versailles

First visited by the Portuguese, who finding it uninhabited and rude in appearance named it Los Barbudos and then abandoned it. Sir William Courteen fitted out two large ships, one of which arrived and formed James' (or Hole) Town
Earl of Carlisle obtained a grant from Charles I of all the Caribbee Islands
Sixty-four settlers arrived in Carlisle Bay, commenced the erection of wooden houses, threw a bridge across the river, and laid the foundation of Bridgetown
Islands derive their name from Bermudez, a Spaniard, who sighted them
First colonized by Admiral Sir George Somers, who was shipwrecked here on his way to Virginia
On the abolition of slavery, the local legislature dispensed with the temporary apprenticeship system, entitling slaves to absolute freedom six years sooner than required by Act of Parliament

Large discoveries of gold attracted vast immigration from California. Hudson's Bay Company's trading licence was revoked and the country erected into a Colony by Act of Imperial Parliament (21 & 22 Vict. cap. 99)
Territory first partially settled by the Dutch West India Company
Finally ceded to Great Britain after being restored to the Dutch in 1802 and retaken in 1803
Canada said to have been discovered by Sebastian Cabot
Quebec, the first settlement, was founded
Quebec succumbed to British forces under General Wolfe
The whole territory of Canada was ceded to Great Britain by the Treaty of Paris
Bartholomew de Diaz, a Portuguese commander, discovered the Cape in the reign of John II of Portugal
